display-xl.purpose: Seat count on the merchant screen. Cal Sans, tabular figures.

display-md.purpose: Seat numeral leading every board row. Cal Sans, tabular figures.

display-sm.purpose: Page h1 on merchant screens. Cal Sans.

wordmark.purpose: The where2go wordmark in top nav and footer. Cal Sans.

title-sm.purpose: Cafe name on a board row; step-button label size.

body-sm.purpose: Notices, field errors, status and foot lines, footer copy.

caption.purpose: Column header and the /total beside a numeral; row meta uses the size at weight 400.

shadows.name: subtle
shadows.purpose: Under the active sort tab only, lifting the white pill off its gray track.

shadows.name: input-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Paired with an ink border on a focused text input; drawn in error red (#ef4444) when the input is invalid.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve; used by both the rank slide and the changed-row wash.

motion.name: rank-slide
motion.purpose: Signature interaction. When the ranking changes, each row animates translateY from its old position to its new one so a cafe is seen moving, not jumping. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: changed-wash
motion.purpose: A row whose count changed fades to surface-card and back. The fade is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; the wash itself still appears.

motion.name: changed-hold
motion.purpose: How long a changed row keeps its surface-card wash and 'was N' in the meta line.

narrative.overview:
where2go reads like a departures board for cafe seats. Every line leads with the number of seats free, set large in Cal Sans with tabular figures, and everything else about the cafe sits beside it in quiet Inter. The canvas is white, ink and actions are near-black, rows are separated by hairlines, and the only chromatic colour on a screen is the small dot that says how full a cafe is.

The system is built for two people in a hurry: someone on the street choosing where to go, and someone behind a counter with seconds to spare. Density is compact on the board (eight rows in a 390px-wide first viewport) and generous on the merchant screen, where the two step buttons are the largest things after the count. Depth is flat. Tone changes, not shadows, separate the column header, the sort switch, the merchant panel, and a row that has just changed. The page always closes on the one dark surface, the footer.

Motion exists to explain a change, never to decorate. When a cafe's count changes, its row slides to its new rank and stays marked with its previous value, so the reader sees what moved and from where.
keyCharacteristics: The free-seat numeral is the first thing read on every line; the cafe name is second.
White canvas, near-black ink and actions, hairline rules, one dark footer.
Cal Sans for the wordmark, seat numerals, and page h1 only; Inter everywhere else.
Status hues live in a 10px dot and are always backed by a numeral and a text label.
Every count shows its age; an unconfirmed count goes muted with a hollow ring.
Flat surfaces; the single shadow in the system sits under the active sort tab.
Every control has a 44px hit area; press states only, no hover styling.

rules.name: The Occupancy-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red mean how full a cafe is and nothing else. They appear as the 10px status dot; red additionally marks an invalid input. They are never button fills, backgrounds, badges, or decoration.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: A status dot is always accompanied by the seat numeral and a text label ("Plenty of room", "Filling up", "Almost full", "Full", "Not confirmed recently"), visible on the merchant screen and screen-reader-only on the board. An unconfirmed count changes shape, not hue: a hollow 2px muted ring.

rules.name: The One Dark Surface Rule
rules.body: The footer is the only near-black surface. Above it, everything is white or a light gray tone.

rules.name: The Numeral Rule
rules.body: Cal Sans is for the wordmark, seat numerals, and page h1. Nothing else. Seat numerals always use tabular figures so a changing count does not shift the columns.

rules.name: The Weight 600 Rule
rules.body: Cal Sans is always weight 600 with negative tracking (-0.5px to -2px, growing with size). Never 700, never untracked.

rules.name: The 44 Rule
rules.body: Every interactive control has a hit area of at least 44px. Buttons and inputs are 44px tall. Where the visible shape is smaller (36px sort tabs, the 36px directions disc), the hit area is extended to 44px around it.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: One shadow exists in the system and it belongs to the active sort tab. Rows, panels, buttons, and inputs never cast one.

dos: Do lead every list line with the free-seat numeral in Cal Sans 600, 2.25rem, tabular figures.
Do show the age of every count next to it, and switch to the hollow muted ring and a muted numeral once it is older than 30 minutes.
Do pair every status dot with a numeral and a text label, visible or screen-reader-only.
Do give every control a 44px hit area, extending it invisibly when the visible shape is 36px.
Do separate with 1px `hairline` rules and tone steps (`surface-soft`, `surface-card`) before reaching for a border box or shadow.
Do keep muted text on `canvas` or `surface-soft`, where it clears 4.5:1; use body colour or ink on `surface-card`.
Do write error copy in `error-text` and keep `error` for the dot and the invalid-input border.
Do keep text inputs at 1rem and buttons at 44px tall on every screen.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing the rank slide and the background fade while keeping the changed mark.
Do end every page with the dark footer.
donts: Don't use Cal Sans for body copy, labels, buttons, cafe names, or empty-state headings; it is for the wordmark, seat numerals, and page h1.
Don't set Cal Sans at any weight other than 600 or without negative tracking.
Don't use green, amber, or red as a button fill, background, badge, or text colour; error copy uses `error-text`.
Don't let colour be the only carrier of occupancy.
Don't add hover styling; controls change on press, focus, and disabled only.
Don't add shadows to rows, panels, buttons, or inputs; the active sort tab owns the only one.
Don't put a dark surface anywhere but the footer.
Don't turn board rows into bordered or rounded cards; the board is hairline-ruled lines.
Don't animate anything that is not explaining a data change.
